VLM-guided gene activity quantification for one sample

Source: R/VIGAT.R
VIGAT.Rd

Draws TSS-centered ATAC coverage plots for each marker gene, asks a vision-language model to select one compact genomic window per gene, and counts fragments in those windows to build a gene-by-cell count matrix. Nothing is written to disk; everything is returned as R objects.

Usage

VIGAT(
  obj,
  genes,
  tissue,
  species = "human",
  cluster_col = NULL,
  min_atac_cluster_cells = 50,
  openai_model = "gpt-5.5",
  return_intermediates = FALSE,
  return_highlighted_plots = FALSE
)

Arguments

obj

A processed Signac Seurat object with an ATAC assay and gene annotation. Set Idents(obj) to the desired ATAC clustering before calling if needed.

genes

Character vector of marker gene names.

tissue

Tissue label injected into the API prompt (e.g. "PBMC").

species

Species label injected into the API prompt (e.g. "human"). Set to NULL to omit from prompt.

cluster_col

Optional. Name of a meta.data column to use as the ATAC cluster assignment. If NULL (default), Idents(obj) is used.

min_atac_cluster_cells

Clusters with fewer cells than this are excluded. Default: 50.

openai_model

OpenAI model name. Default: "gpt-5.5".

return_intermediates

Logical. If TRUE, also return the intermediate results: TSS info, overlapping peaks, the coverage plots sent to the model, the prompt, the full API response and run information. Default: FALSE.

return_highlighted_plots

Logical. If TRUE, also return one coverage plot per gene with the selected window highlighted. Default: FALSE.

Value

A named list:

vigat_windows

GRanges containing VIGAT-selected genomic windows.

vigat_window_df

Data frame containing the selected genomic windows.

count_matrix

Sparse gene-by-cell raw ATAC count matrix generated by counting fragments overlapping the VIGAT-selected windows using Signac::FeatureMatrix().

diagnostics

List containing raw_response, genes_found, and genes_skipped.

intermediates

Only if return_intermediates = TRUE: list with tss_info, overlapping_peaks, coverage_plots (named list of ggplot objects), prompt, api_response and api_run_info.

highlighted_plots

Only if return_highlighted_plots = TRUE: named list of ggplot objects, one per gene.

API key

This function reads the OpenAI API key from the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable. Set it before calling the function:


Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = "your_key_here")

or add it to your ~/.Renviron file:


OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = "your_key_here")
Idents(obj) <- "ATAC_snn_res.0.8"
res <- VIGAT(
  obj     = obj,
  genes   = c("INS", "GCG", "SST"),
  tissue  = "Islet",
  species = "human"
)
res$vigat_window_df

# Keep the highlighted plots and save them yourself
res <- VIGAT(obj, genes = c("INS", "GCG"), tissue = "Islet",
             return_highlighted_plots = TRUE)
for (g in names(res$highlighted_plots)) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(g, "_vigat.png"), res$highlighted_plots[[g]],
                  width = 7, height = 7, dpi = 150)
}
} # }
